High Court judge Eric Kwok Tung-ming on Tuesday handed down the sentence to the 48-year-old defendant, whom he described as lacking “an ounce of kindness” towards his daughter, whom he raped 14... item.title: Indian-origin teen built anti-cyberbullying tech in 2013; now runs non-profit rewarded by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle
item.description: Trisha Prabhu created ReThink, a mobile keyboard preventing cyberbullying by prompting users to reconsider offensive messages. This initiative grew into a global non-profit organization supporting millions of students worldwide. Prabhu's work earned her significant recognition and substantial funding for her impactful efforts. She continues to lead ReThink Citizens, promoting digital wellness and a kinder internet. Her dedication exemplifies how one motivated individual can drive significant positive social change. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Black drongos introduced for pest control later threatened Guam’s native birds
item.description: In 1935, the introduction of black drongos to Rota aimed to control agricultural pests. This effort led to the birds establishing their populations, eventually spreading to Guam. However, their aggressive behavior towards native bird species has contributed significantly to declines in local avian populations, highlighting the unforeseen consequences of introducing non-native species into ecosystems. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: China cut its holdings of US Treasuries to a nearly 18-year low in June, as Beijing continued to diversify its foreign exchange reserves amid heightened geopolitical tensions and growing uncertainty over the policy outlook in the United States. item.title: 3,000-year-old inscription naming Masn may help archaeologists identify the lost Egyptian city
item.description: A remarkable sandstone lintel inscribed with the titles of Ramesses II was uncovered at Tell Abu Seify. This inscription reveals valuable information about the restoration of a statue of Horus, the Lord of Masn. Such findings bolster the theory that this site may very well be the fabled lost city of Masn, showcasing evolution from a significant religious and military hub to an industrial quarry through recent excavations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
